title: Three Indians Rescued in Thailand After Being Lured With Fake Tour Package and Held for Ransom
excerpt: Five suspects arrested in Bangkok after the victims were tortured in a Pattaya house and their families asked to pay ₹40 lakh each, with the operation traced to a Pakistan-based mastermind in Dubai.
body:
• Three Indian men aged 20 to 24 were lured to Thailand with a cheap seven-day tour package, then held captive and tortured in a house in Pattaya.
  • The kidnappers demanded ₹40 lakh (~$47,000) per victim from their families and used fake blood on video calls to pressure payment.
  • Thai police rescued all three victims on Monday and arrested five Indian suspects in Bangkok's Khlong Tan area on Tuesday.
  • The operation was directed by a Pakistani national based in Dubai who communicated through encrypted apps and demanded ransom via cryptocurrency.

Lured to Pattaya With a Cheap Package

Three young Indian men — Mohit, 23, Ashish, 24, and Himanshu, 20 — traveled to Thailand after being offered what appeared to be a bargain seven-day tour package. Instead of a vacation, they walked into a trap. Upon arriving in Pattaya, the men were taken to a house where they were held captive, according to Thai police.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2082372342504972511

The victims told investigators they were kept hungry for days, had their hands and feet bound, were beaten, and were hung upside down. To increase pressure on their families, the captors sprayed red paint on the victims' bodies to simulate bleeding injuries during video calls.

Each family was told to pay ₹40 lakh (approximately $47,000) for the release of their relative, bringing the total ransom demand to ₹1.2 crore.

"They applied red spray paint on the victims' bodies so that during video calls it would appear that they had sustained serious injuries and were bleeding."

— Thai police statement

Indian Embassy Triggers Rescue

The breakthrough came when the victims' families contacted the Indian Embassy in Bangkok. The embassy immediately alerted Chonburi Immigration and Pattaya Police on July 21. After a coordinated investigation, Thai police rescued all three men on Monday evening.

The following day, officers arrested five Indian nationals in Bangkok's Khlong Tan area: Avtar Singh, 38, Jagjit Singh, 38, Rambhalak Kumar, 24, Sukhbir Singh, 37, and Kulra Singh, 27. During interrogation, the suspects revealed they had been receiving instructions from a Pakistani national based in Dubai through an encrypted messaging application for about a month before the kidnapping.

The Dubai-based mastermind wanted the ransom paid through cryptocurrency, making the money trail harder to trace. Thai authorities are now working with international agencies to pursue the case across borders.

A Growing Pattern of Crime Against Indian Travelers

The case is not isolated. Thailand has seen a string of incidents involving Indian nationals being targeted for kidnapping, scams, and extortion in recent years. In April 2025, four Indian nationals were rescued from a house in Bangkok's Yannawa district in a similar ransom scheme, with captors demanding 2.5 million rupees. In May 2026, Thai immigration police arrested an Indian fugitive wanted for kidnapping and drug trafficking who had fled to Bangkok.

The pattern has prompted growing concern about the safety of Indian tourists in Southeast Asia, particularly those who book travel through informal or unverified channels. India was Thailand's fourth-largest source of tourists in 2025, with over 2 million visitors.

Travel Advisory Implications

While Thailand remains a popular and largely safe destination for Indian travelers, the incident highlights the risks of booking through unfamiliar agents or responding to offers that seem too good to be true. The Indian Embassy in Bangkok has repeatedly urged citizens to use licensed tour operators and register their travel with the embassy.

Indian travelers in Thailand can reach the embassy's emergency helpline at +66-81-837-3353. The Ministry of External Affairs also operates a 24/7 helpline at +91-11-40503000 for Indians in distress abroad.

Thai police have filed charges against the five suspects under sections of the Thai Criminal Code covering unlawful detention and ransom, which carry penalties including life imprisonment.
nri_angle: Three young Indian men were kidnapped while traveling in Thailand, underscoring safety risks for Indian tourists abroad and the role of Indian embassies in coordinating rescues.
